# Pottery

Curated by Skill Harbor — a complete wheel-throwing guide: prerequisites (wheel, clay body, tools, kiln access), wedging technique, centering with anchored elbows, opening, pulling walls with even pressure, shaping, cutting off, trimming a foot ring, pulling and attaching handles, bisque and glaze firing with ramp guidance, and a common-mistakes section (fighting the wheel, dry hands, fast pulls, uneven drying). Honest about the learning curve: 20–50 hours of practice minimum to develop the feel. References real sources (Ceramics: A Potter's Handbook, Mastering Cone 6 Glazes, Orton cone chart) and ships with a cone-chart reference file. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @joshrotenberg. Honest caveats: no digital prerequisites, but you need real equipment — a wheel, clay, and kiln access (a community studio membership with shelf space); Muse can coach the technique, not replace practice; 1 install on the catalog, but popularity is not a review. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
